title: HSM-KMS compatibility matrix + Terraform appendix (v0.1 draft)
content:
Purpose
This doc is a working appendix: compatibility matrix for supported HSMs/KMS backends, pragmatic Terraform notes for private/on-prem installs, and an upgrade + rollback checklist focusing on security hardening (KMS/HSM integration, secrets lifecycle, envelope encryption and audit log retention).

Summary notes (top-line)
- Goal: provide a reproducible, low-risk path to (1) onboard vendor HSMs into our Private control plane, (2) upgrade TF modules that manage KMS/HSM bindings, and (3) ensure audit logs + key rotation are preserved for compliance.
- Audience: infra engineers, SRE, security/ops, and professional services doing private/on-prem installs.
- Status: v0.1 draft — experiment notes and commands; intended to be refined into a playbook (v1.0) after 2 pilot installs.

Compatibility matrix (operational focus)
- Thales Luna (Luna SA 8.x / 9.x): PKCS#11 primary, KMIP addon available. Tested with our PKCS#11 shim (kms-adapter v0.9). Recommended firmware >= 9.1.3 for stable multi-part key import.
- AWS CloudHSM (clustered): PKCS#11 interface. Note: network topology must allow TCP 2225/2226 between HSM client nodes and HSM cluster. Use dedicated VLAN. Verified: TLS handshake with SoftHSM not reliable for all key attributes; use official libs.
- YubiHSM 2 / YubiHSM SDK: constrained device (no large RSA > 2048), ideal for signing/sealing small secrets. Not suitable for bulk envelope encryption; used as certificate/attestation anchor.
- Gemalto/SafeNet (older models): KMIP preferred; PKCS#11 supported but some older firmware lacks CKM_AES_GCM. Avoid for new installs unless firmware upgrade available.
- SoftHSM (dev/test): supports PKCS#11; do not use in prod. Use only for CI test harness.

Mapping decisions (what we picked)
- Production default: PKCS#11 for Luna/CloudHSM when low-latency symmetric ops needed; KMIP for management planes where vendor offers it.
- Attestation and anchor keys: require HSM-backed asymmetric keys stored on device (YubiHSM acceptable in attestation role).
- Envelope encryption flow: data key (DEK) generated in KMS (or HSM), wrapped with HSM KEK using AES-GCM when supported. Fallback: wrap with software KMS with HSM-stored master if device lacks AES-GCM.

Terraform appendix (practical notes)
- Module layout recommendations:
  - modules/kms-hsm/README.md: operational vars, expected secrets, and required provider versions.
  - modules/kms-hsm/main.tf: minimal resources: local provider configs, null_resource for keyimport scripts (see below), data blocks for certificate pins.
- Provider versions:
  - pin terraform provider aws >= 5.0 for CloudHSM resources.
  - Use hashicorp/null v3.x for orchestration steps. Avoid relying on random provider behaviors during upgrades.
- State handling:
  - Keep resources that reference HSM device metadata in a separate state file (state file per site). Reason: device renames / IP changes should not risk global state.
  - Enable state locking (consul/remote backend) and short lock TTL during key import operations.
- Example variables (operational):
  - hsm_vendor = "luna" | "cloudhsm" | "yubihsm"
  - hsm_endpoint = "10.0.7.12:2225"
  - hsm_pkcs11_lib = "/opt/lunaclient/lib/libCryptoki2_64.so"
  - kms_key_alias = "redwood/siteX/master"
  - wrap_algorithm_preference = "AES-GCM"
- Onboarding script pattern (invoked by null_resource.local-exec):
  - preflight: ssh to management host, ensure HSM SDK installed, pkcs11-tool --list-slots returns slot with token label expected.
  - key creation: call vendor CLI to create a key with attributes: non-exportable, symmetric, AES-256, allowed for keyWrap/unWrap.
  - export-wrap: if vendor supports wrap directly, instruct HSM to export wrapped DEK to import into local KMS store; else generate DEK inside HSM and store wrapped copy to S3.
  - register: call control-plane api to register key thumbprint and endpoints.
  - smoke test: sign a sample payload and verify on control-plane verification path.

Upgrade plan (Terraform module bump + HSM binding)
- Preconditions:
  - Designated maintenance window (2 hours) per site; SRE on pager, oncall contact, and communications doc prepared.
  - Backup: snapshot Terraform state + database backup + export of wrapped keys to secure S3 bucket (encrypted, separate retention).
  - Stakeholders: eng-private-deployments, eng-sre, security.
- Steps (zero-downtime objective where possible):
  1) Push terraform module code to branch and open PR (see linked PR). Run plan in staging state.
  2) Validate: run terraform plan with -var-file=siteX.tfvars against staging state. Verify no destructive ops for existing HSM key objects.
  3) If plan changes provider blocks (provider version bumps), prepare to run in a canary site first.
  4) Acquire exclusive lock on site state.
  5) Run terraform apply targeting only modules/kms-hsm (use -target when needed).
  6) Run the onboarding script (null_resource triggers) to import or create keys on HSM device. Monitor logs (see Audit logs section).
  7) Run acceptance tests: encrypt/decrypt cycle, envelope unwrap, cross-node verification.
  8) Promote changes to other sites sequentially.
- Rollback plan:
  - If key import fails: automated cleanup script deletes partially created transient keys (where vendor supports). Revert the terraform apply using the saved snapshot or run terraform apply to restore previous resources from state snapshot.
  - If control-plane fails to accept new key: re-register previous wrapped key and restore service flows.
  - If unable to rollback: escalate to oncall and enact emergency fallback: switch to software-wrapped KEK stored in cloud KMS (only for dedicated-hosted fallback, requires approval). Document this as incident activity.

Secrets lifecycle and rotation notes
- Principle: DEKs are ephemeral per-object; KEKs (HSM-backed) are long-lived and rotated carefully.
- Rotation strategy: use dual-key acceptance window: new KEK imported and registered, both old and new KEK accepted for unwrap for a 7-day acceptance window, then old KEK retired.
- Automation: rotation runbook (cron job via control-plane) should: create new KEK, copy/wrap existing DEKs (or rewrap on first access), and update metadata in the keystore.
- CI/CD secrets: CI should use short-lived bootstrap tokens that can only request attestation (no secret material). Do not place pkcs11_lib paths in shared repos.

Audit logs and retention (compliance-focused)
- Required events to capture:
  - Key creation/import/destruction, wrap/unwrap operations, admin role changes, key attribute modifications, firmware updates, and HSM connectivity failures.
- Pipeline:
  - HSM syslog -> site fluentd instance (TLS) -> s3://redwood-audit/siteX/raw/ -> lambda/process -> elasticsearch/siem for alerts.
  - Ensure logs are tamper-evident: we add an HMAC chain per daily file with a root-key stored in HSM (attestation-only key) so we can prove non-modification.
- Retention: default 7 years for production customer sites (configurable), with 30-day hot window for SIEM analysis.

Acceptance tests and smoke checklist
- Pre-upgrade:
  - PKCS#11 list-slots and vendor CLI verify token presence.
  - local control-plane can authenticate to HSM with admin creds.
  - Baseline latency metric for wrap/unwrap recorded.
- Post-upgrade:
  - All services can create, wrap, and unwrap DEKs.
  - No increased failure rate in 1-hour canary window.
  - Audit events recorded for each key import and match expected schema.

Operational pitfalls (collected from pilots)
- Device clock skew caused certificate verification failures — ensure NTP in management VLAN.
- Long-running pkcs11 sessions --> vendor resource exhaustion; use short sessions and reuse contexts when possible.
- Firmware update that silently changes attribute defaults; always test firmware updates on a lab unit first.
- Terraform drift: vendor CLIs sometimes create objects that TF cannot import properly — prefer import path in plan and document import IDs.

Open items / TODOs
- [ ] Create canonical terraform module README with per-vendor examples and expected import ids (owner: Jonah).
- [ ] Add encrypted transfer checklist for wrapped keys between customer site and our S3 staging (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Confluence page: standard audit schema + examples (owner: Mariana).
- [ ] Implement CI smoke harness using SoftHSM that simulates AES-GCM unwrap times under load (owner: Ethan).

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- List pkcs11 slots:
  pkcs11-tool --module /opt/lunaclient/lib/libCryptoki2_64.so -L
- Create symmetric key (vendor CLI pseudo):
  vendor-cli create-key --type symmetric --algo AES --size 256 --flags wrap,unwrap --label "redwood-siteX-kek"
- Terraform import example:
  terraform import module.kms-hsm.hsm_key.site_kek "vendor://token/label/1234"
- Basic audit query (elastic):
  GET /audit/_search?q=event:unwrap AND site:siteX&size=50

Contacts and escalation
- eng-private-deployments Slack: #eng-private-deployments
- Oncall SRE: pager -> SRE rotation (see rota doc)
- Security escalation: security@redwood.ai (pager for incident severity >= sev2)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally operational and prescriptive; feedback needed on the module boundaries and whether we should require per-site state-files by default. Looking for pilot volunteers (2 customer sites) to sanity check timelines.

End of draft
